title: Text needs enough contrast with its background
summary: Text color is too close to the background color to read comfortably. Darken the text or lighten the background until it reaches 4.5 to 1.
problem: The color of some text is too similar to the color behind it. WCAG asks for a contrast ratio of at least 4.5 to 1 for normal text, and at least 3 to 1 for large text (about 24px, or 19px bold). The light gray #999999 on white measures 2.85 to 1, so it fails.
whoItAffects: People with low vision or color vision deficiency, and older readers whose eyes need more contrast. Anyone reading on a phone in bright sunlight or on a dim screen is affected too.
whyItMatters: Text people cannot read might as well not be on the page: prices, delivery notes and form hints go unseen. This is a WCAG 1.4.3 failure at Level AA, the level that accessibility regulations and procurement requirements commonly build on.
steps: Find the text and its colors in the scan result, which names the foreground color, the background color and the ratio measured.
Darken the text color or lighten the background color until the ratio reaches 4.5 to 1. For large text, 3 to 1 is enough.
Check the new pair in a contrast checker before you change your stylesheet or theme settings. For example, #595959 on white measures 7.00 to 1.
Change the color once in a shared CSS rule or theme setting, so every place that uses it is fixed together.
Check text over images and gradients at the lightest and darkest points behind it. Add a solid or semi-opaque panel behind the text if needed.
howToCheck: Open your browser's developer tools, inspect the text and look at the contrast value in the color picker. Or paste the two hex colors into a contrast checker and compare against 4.5 to 1.
